transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-31
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood CSM), Maya (AstraHealth - Head of ML), Carlos (Infra), Dana (CTO), Jasper (SRE)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync to review latest benchmark results we ran overnight (Redwood vs baseline vendor VendorX), discuss tuning (batching, KV cache, quantization) and agree next steps for the pilot. Some measurement noise but overall Redwood shows lower p50 latency and better throughput at target concurrency after tuning. Security docs and perf logs to be shared.

Topics covered:
- Benchmark results: p50/p95 latency, throughput (requests per second), token/sec cost estimate
- Configuration: batching window, max batch size, KV cache hit rate, quantization profile used (int8 vs int4-ish), model variant
- Infrastructure: GPU type, autoscaling, VPC/private deployment considerations
- Next steps & action items: share CSVs, infra deep dive, security docs

Transcript:
0:00 Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this to 45, quick recap of last week and then go through the numbers, lena you want to kick off with the runs?
0:12 Lena: yeah, sure, so we ran the two production-like gait runs overnight, both 1k concurrent simulated users, 30s think time, we compared Redwood-hosted optimized runtime against their baseline VendorX Cloud instance using the same model family, approximate size 13B. note: some tokenization differences so numbers are approximations.
0:30 Maya: quick question before you go too deep, which model variant did you use? we asked for the parity one, right?
0:36 Lena: yep, we used the parity-compat variant, same checkpoints, we also tried a quantized int8 profile on Redwood and a mixed float on VendorX to be conservative.
0:48 Carlos: and hardware parity? what GPUs were in the baseline?
0:51 Lena: VendorX was running A100-40 configs (single node per process), Redwood run used A10G for batch tests and also an A100-80 run for a direct compare in the cost perimeter, we noted that for the A10G run Redwood still outperformed on throughput due to continuous batching and prefix KV caching.
1:10 Jasper: we saw earlier you mentioned KV cache hit rates — what were they in the run?
1:14 Lena: cache hit was around 68% in the Redwood throughput run; for VendorX baseline the equivalent was about 12% because their setup didn't do prefix caching across requests in this config. that matters a lot for our use case since you have lots of repeated prompt prefixes.
1:30 Maya: ok makes sense, numbers? p50/p95?
1:34 Lena: ok raw numbers, approximate: Redwood p50 latency 120ms, p95 420ms for the 13B parity-variant on A100-80 with batching tuned; VendorX p50 210ms, p95 750ms on their baseline config. Throughput: Redwood delivered ~850 req/s sustained on the test harness, VendorX ~420 req/s. note these are end-to-end token generation latencies, test set 32 token avg.
2:00 Dana: that's a big delta, is this mostly caching or kernel selection?
2:04 Lena: a few factors — continuous batching & dynamic kernel selection reduced per-token overhead, plus KV cache. we also applied quantization-friendly kernel paths so int8 gave ~18% lower token-cost vs VendorX mixed float in our runs. but for 95th we still see tail variance related to GC/queue spikes on VendorX.
2:26 Maya: did you run a strict parity test where both used same GPU family and same quantization?
2:30 Lena: yes, the A100-80 parity runs had both on A100, same quant profile int8, Redwood p50 108ms p95 390ms vs VendorX p50 150ms p95 610ms. so still a gap.
2:45 Carlos: what's the memory footprint with int8 + kv caching? any OOM concerns?
2:50 Lena: int8 lowered model vram by about 40%, kv cache for this workload used ~6GB per shard, our shard sizing still leaves margin on A100-80. we did a couple of stress runs and didn't see OOMs, but we need to validate with your 512-token tail cases.
3:05 Jasper: you mentioned batching windows — what's the tradeoff you're tuning?
3:08 Lena: we tuned a 20ms micro-batching window which increased throughput and only added ~18ms to p50; we can tighten for lower SLOs if you care about absolute p50. it's a knob — latency vs cost.
3:22 Maya: cost numbers? even rough delta vs VendorX would help for execs
3:27 Samir: rough math from the benchmark: token unit cost estimate shows Redwood about 22% cheaper at current batch/kv settings because you get higher utilization (fewer idle cycles) and the int8 path reduces GPU hours. we'll send a CSV with cost-per-1M-tokens extrapolation.
3:45 Dana: any stability regressions or failures in the overnight runs?
3:48 Lena: one transient spike at 02:13 UTC — a queue backlog because we changed batch size mid-run, we've annotated logs. otherwise success rate 99.96% on Redwood, VendorX 99.8 in their run, small sample but consistent with tail differences.
4:05 Maya: how confident are you about the production mapping? our traffic has lots of shorter prompts and some long assistant flows, will caching help?
4:12 Lena: caching helps a lot on shorter repeated prefixes, less so for highly unique long prompts. we can run a second set with your sample traffic; Maya, if you can send the sample prompt set we'll re-run with TTL and real sequence lengths.
4:26 Maya: yes will send.
4:28 Carlos: about private deployment — we still need VPC and KMS; any perf delta for private?
4:34 Samir: good question — private VPC control plane doesn't affect inference runtime if you use Redwood Dedicated in your VPC; we did see ~5-8% higher latency when we tested on our self-hosted on-prem variant due to network egress but for your Dedicated/hosted VPC it'll be comparable. we'll document network hops.
4:52 Maya: security docs, SOC2 etc?
4:54 Ravi: I'll share SOC2, ISO attestation link and redwood private deployment architecture doc right after — same day.
4:59 Maya: great.
5:00 Jasper: curious about failover — if a model shard goes down does Redwood automatically route to a compatible variant?
5:07 Lena: yes, our smart routing can fallback to a lower-capacity variant or another region; in the POC we enabled automatic fallback to the 13B quantized variant with little quality loss, that did add a small latency bump but kept availability.
5:20 Carlos: what about telemetry and per-route cost breakdown, can we get token-level cost per route?
5:25 Samir: yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdown per route. we'll give you a demo view with the POC metrics.
5:34 Maya: a quick note on VendorX — they told us they could do similar caching but we couldn't replicate that behavior in their managed config; maybe it's available as a separate module but it wasn't enabled in baseline.
5:46 Dana: ok, sounds reasonable. any blockers to proceed?
5:50 Samir: nothing blocking — main asks are your sample prompt set and confirmation on GPU family you'd like us to test at parity. also we'll send the CSV, logs, and security pack.
6:03 Maya: timeline for the infra deep-dive?
6:06 Lena: propose Friday 09/04 for a 60min session to go into kernel selection, quantization tradeoffs, and autoscale configs.
6:14 Maya: works for me.
6:15 Carlos: I'll join, will invite SRE.
6:17 Samir: excellent. I'll also attach the benchmark plots and raw CSV in the follow-up email.
6:22 Maya: one last thing — for exec summary, can you provide a short slide with key numbers (p50/p95/throughput/cost-delta) and callouts on assumptions?
6:31 Samir: yep, we'll do a one-pager slide and a single CSV.
6:35 Dana: thank you, this was helpful.
6:37 Samir: thanks all — recap of next steps: Samir send CSV & slides, Lena schedule infra deep dive, Ravi send security docs, Maya provide sample prompt traffic. we'll sync again next week same time.
6:56 End of call.
